messages:
Sam: heads up, eu-west1 started showing a creeping pile of tiny-pod Pending around 03:10 UTC. not classic fragmentation — scheduler seems to skip warm nodes intermittently after the NIC firmware roll yesterday.
Ben: saw that. noticed bind timeouts in the scheduler logs + a few node-label sync errors.
Priya: do we have an alert that groups Pending by node-age?
Miguel: DevBot triggered an alert: "Pending spike: ml namespace > 100 pods (5m)" at 03:12
Ben: quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep Pending | wc -l` -> 118 at 03:15. many are tiny gpu=0.125 requests.
Sam: exact pattern: lots of small replica sets (batch jobs) landing in queue, scheduler prefers nodes with specific gpu-labels but those labels were slow to reconcile after the NIC patch -> pack signal lag.
Priya: temp mitigation idea: increase warm-pool size for eu-west1 by +10 small slots and run a descheduler pass to coalesce tiny pods onto warm nodes. low friction and reversible.
Miguel: i'm worried about cost — adding 10 warm slots increases committed GPUs by ~0.3% this month. acceptable for a 2h mitigation?
ops-oncall: agree with Priya for now. can we do a canary: bump 2 slots first and measure pending drop?
Ben: also recommend flipping scheduler tuning: reduce `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` weight on gpu-affinity for tiny-pods so they don't block larger gangs. takes effect immediately.
Sam: good call. Priya can you run the descheduler dry-run and share the plan?
Priya: running dry-run now -> `descheduler --policy-config /etc/descheduler/policy.yaml --evict-local-storage=false --dry-run=true`
Priya: dry-run output: would migrate ~92 tiny pods to warm nodes, free ~14 full-gpu slots for larger jobs.
Miguel: nice. timeline to actual run?
Priya: execute in 10m if no objections. will also patch scheduler config to lower affinity weight at the same time.
Ben: one more short-term: add a node-label-sync job to reapply gpu labels every 30s for 5m after firmware events. avoids recurrence until NIC rollout is stable.
Sam: let's do staged approach: +2 warm slots now, descheduler dry-run, if pending drops by >50% in 5m then bump remainder +8 and apply scheduler weight tweak and label-sync job.
ops-oncall: running the +2 warm slots patch: `infractl scale warmpool --region=eu-west1 --gpu-shape=small --add=2`
DevBot: infractl: started scaling warmpool eu-west1 (+2 small) — job id 67823.
Priya: executing descheduler (non-dry): `descheduler --policy-config /etc/descheduler/policy.yaml --evict-local-storage=false`
Miguel: monitoring pending count... 03:30 -> 64 pending (down from 118).
Ben: great signal. go ahead with +8 and scheduler tweak.
Priya: applying scheduler tweak: patching ConfigMap `kube-scheduler` weight gpuAffinity=60 -> 30.
Sam: also opened a follow-up runbook ticket to track root cause of label reconciliation slowness after NIC firmware: infra/FP-2301.
Miguel: cost note for finance: temporary warmpool bump ~0.3% this month, but we reclaimed 14 full-gpu slots so net user-impact avoided.
ops-oncall: after the changes, evictions dropped and larger jobs resumed. keeping descheduler in weekly cron for another week.
Ben: long-term: we should consider making the label-sync idempotent in the agent so firmware rolls don't cause transient scheduling gaps. filing infra-ops backlog item.
Sam: thanks team. if anyone sees the pending count spike again, ping on-call and I'll re-open throttles. :thumbsup:
Priya: adding brief summary to the incident channel and tagging on-call for 24h watch.
DevBot: Incident note: 2026-03-21 eu-west1 tiny-pod-surge mitigated by warmpool scaling + descheduler + scheduler-tweak.
